bullets.title: MRVL +10%: Google expands AI chip partnership with $12.2B warrant deal
bullets.body: Marvell issued Google a warrant for up to 58.97M shares at $206.58 (strike), with full vesting implying ~$120B in cumulative Google purchases over ~7 years. The expanded partnership covers custom AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, and near-memory compute for the TPU ecosystem. Oppenheimer maintains Outperform, noting the deal validates MRVL's XPU guidance to double to $4B+ next year before reaching $10B+ in CY28; MRVL added ~$17B of equity value on the day, closing around $235.

bullets.title: AVGO: Google-Marvell deal viewed as incremental negative, not existential threat
bullets.body: JPM explicitly notes the Google-Marvell deal should NOT be viewed as negative for AVGO; AVGO remains Google's primary TPU partner with a 5-year LTA through 2031 signed April 2026 and is ramping six other major projects (META, OpenAI, Anthropic). Analysts remain buyers of both MRVL and AVGO. Broadcom fell 4.6% on the day amid initial concern, but the deal is framed as an 'attach to TPU ecosystem' rather than displacement.

bullets.title: ADI: Record $4B quarter; UBS reiterates Buy at $490, Bernstein upgrades to Outperform
bullets.body: ADI reported Q3 revenue of $4.02B and non-GAAP EPS of $3.45 (top of guidance range); Q4 guided to $4.30B (+7% vs normal +5% seasonality) with gross margin expanding ~150bps to ~74%. Data Center revenue surged 95%+ Y/Y; ADI estimates $1.0-1.5B per GW of analog opportunity in AI infrastructure. Bernstein upgraded to Outperform with a $465 PT (25% upside); KeyBanc maintains Overweight at $525; UBS reiterates Buy at $490. Channel inventory remains below target with no restocking signals.

bullets.title: INTU: Mizuho cutting estimates/PT ahead of FQ4; debrief call Aug 25
bullets.body: Mizuho expects INTU's FQ4 results to trigger a reset to expectations and is reducing estimates and price target ahead of the August 25 earnings. Analyst is hosting a post-earnings debrief at 8:30 PM ET that evening.

bullets.title: MU: S&P upgrades credit rating to BBB+ with positive outlook on demand recovery
bullets.body: S&P Global raised Micron Technology's credit rating to BBB+ with a positive outlook, citing higher confidence in near-term demand recovery. No price target or equity rating action accompanies the credit upgrade.

bullets.title: NVDA: Facilitating Nordic data-center matchmaking; weighing $20B investment in AI data supplier Mercor
bullets.body: Nvidia is brokering deals between GPU customers and Nordic data-center operators to accelerate AI infrastructure deployment in the region (power, land, cooling advantages). Separately, NVDA is in discussions to invest in Mercor, an AI training data supplier, at a $20B valuation, consistent with Bloomberg's July reports. NVDA CDS hedging is 100% hedge fund-led per MS credit desk; NVDA/SpaceX expected to be added to CDX IG47 with ~95% probability at the next roll.

bullets.title: AMD: Engineers integrating directly into NVDA's NIXL library; 2030 rack claims 570x MI300X performance
bullets.body: AMD engineers are now landing code directly into NVIDIA's NIXL upstream inference communications library, eliminating monthly sync overhead—a notable shift after a decade of NVIDIA blocking AMD contributions. Separately, AMD claims its 2030 AI racks will match 570 MI300X racks using just 2 racks and slash power consumption 20x.

bullets.title: INTC down while market rallies; bullish options flow noted alongside weakness
bullets.body: INTC was one of the few stocks declining on a broad market up day. Separately, options flow data showed INTC among the most bullish flow names earlier in the session, creating a conflicting near-term signal.

bullets.title: SNOW: UBS CFO survey sees dedicated data warehouse instances as AI pull-through beneficiary
bullets.body: UBS surveyed CFOs and found AI token spend ramping 20x per developer since year-end 2025, with 50-100% spending growth planned through year-end 2026. CFOs are planning dedicated data warehouse instances (e.g., Snowflake) for AI-enabled FP&A, representing a key data-layer pull-through theme. SNOW also appeared on Hedgeye's top-30 signal strength longs for Aug 19.

bullets.title: LOW: Mixed Q2; FY26 guidance lowered; KeyBanc Overweight $275, Mizuho raises PT to $250
bullets.body: LOW reported Q2 comps +0.2% (missed HD for first time in ~1 year), with online sales +15.7%. FY26 guidance lowered citing DIY weakness, supply chain costs, and 10Y yield headwinds (now ~4.64% vs ~4.05% in February). KeyBanc maintains Overweight at $275 PT; Mizuho raises PT to $250 (from $280) on ~18x FY28E, noting $80M in IEEPA tariff refunds received with more to flow.

bullets.title: ADBE: BofA raises PT to $220 from $190
bullets.body: BofA Global Research raised Adobe's price target to $220 from $190. No rating change mentioned in available content.

bullets.title: BILL: FQ4 beat; FY27 revenue guide below consensus at +11-14%
bullets.body: BILL reported FQ4 revenue of $436M (vs $431M consensus) and non-GAAP operating income of $102M (vs $85M consensus). FY27 core revenue guidance of +11-14% YoY came in below the +14% consensus, though FY27 profitability outlook of ~24% margin beat expectations at 22%. Mizuho maintains Neutral. BILL repurchased 8M shares in FQ4 for $300M.

bullets.title: HOOD +4.6%, AFRM +5.1% on crypto regulatory tailwinds and CLARITY Act progress
bullets.body: HOOD gained 4.6% and AFRM gained 5.1% as Senate confirmed a September vote for the CLARITY Act. COIN surged 9.5% on the same catalyst. Banking index fell 2.1% while rate-sensitive fintech names outperformed on bull-flattening following Treasury's announced buyback expansion.

bullets.title: UBER +4.6% on autonomous rides launch in Europe
bullets.body: UBER gained 4.6% on the day following the launch of autonomous rides in Europe. Internet sector led the broader tech complex with a +2.1% gain.

bullets.title: RCL: Hedgeye upgrades to top of best-ideas list; sees path to ~$400+
bullets.body: Hedgeye upgraded Royal Caribbean to the top of its best-ideas list, calling Q3 yield weakness temporary and flagging Q4 yield inflection with 2027-28 as the real upside catalysts. Same-ship pricing growth, new ship additions, and shoreside revenue drivers (beach clubs, river cruising) support the $400+ price path. Hedgeye cites AI-driven search tailwinds and growing direct booking mix as additional factors.

bullets.title: DKNG: PA sports betting GGR surges 33% YoY in July with 33% handle share
bullets.body: DraftKings captured 33% of Pennsylvania sports betting handle in July (up from 27%), with GGR +33% YoY. FanDuel posted +26% GGR YoY, while Caesars declined 11% YoY. iGaming revenue across PA grew +9% YoY; overall casino floor revenue was flat YoY.

bullets.title: U (Unity): Wolfe Research discontinues coverage; prior rating Peer Perform
bullets.body: Wolfe Research dropped coverage of Unity Software due to analyst resource reallocation. Prior rating was Peer Perform; current price $46.74, market cap $20.6B, 9.7% short interest. Final estimates should no longer be relied upon.

bullets.title: GS TMT desk: AI momentum under pressure; broadening trade gaining traction ahead of NVDA earnings
bullets.body: GS TMT Momentum Pair fell 9% in two sessions as market leadership inverted (Small > Big, Low Vol > High Vol). The desk sees the AI theme as increasingly two-way, with the inference/media/internet diversity trade gaining vs. pure-play semis. Upcoming key events: CRDO and AVGO earnings near-term, NVDA and DELL shortly after, followed by out-of-favor software (WDAY, CRM, ADBE, INTU). JPM raises 2026 S&P 500 target to 8,000 and maintains tactical bullish view.

bullets.title: OpenAI ARR hits ~$45B (35% QTD growth); sequential growth slowing; IPO by 2027
bullets.body: OpenAI's CFO reported ARR grew from ~$33B (June 30) to ~$44.5B (August 18), representing 35% QTD growth with enterprise revenue up 50% QTD. However, monthly sequential growth slowed to 11% in August vs 22% in July. AI coding products hit 20M weekly active users. Token monetization is declining due to aggressive price cuts. IPO targeted for 2027 at the latest, potentially sooner. OpenAI's Q2 losses widened despite sequential revenue growth, indicating margin pressure from compute/infra scaling.

bullets.title: AMZN: Prime Air drone delivery expanding to ~500 US cities by end of 2026
bullets.body: Amazon plans to expand its Prime Air drone delivery program to nearly 500 US cities and towns by end of 2026, adding Georgia, Ohio, Illinois, Idaho, and New York to its current seven-state footprint. No guidance impact commentary provided.
